title: Wrong date and time breaks websites
symptom: Websites show 'Your connection is not private' warnings
user_description: Every website is showing a scary warning about my connection not being private. Even the ones I use every day.

options.text: Tell him to click 'proceed anyway' on every warning
options.why: Teaches users to ignore security warnings, which can lead to real attacks. Find the cause instead.

options.text: Turn off secure connections in the browser
options.why: Removes protection for every site. Never weaken security to hide a warning.

options.text: Check and correct the date, time and time zone, turn on automatic time sync, and if it keeps resetting suspect the small battery on the motherboard
options.why: Secure sites check certificates against the PC's clock, so a wrong date makes them look invalid. Fixing the time and syncing it solves it, and a repeatedly resetting clock points to a worn clock battery.
Wasteful. A wrong clock is a simple setting to fix.

hints: What would make every site look untrustworthy at the same time?
How does a secure site know whether its certificate is still valid?
What if the clock keeps losing the right time?
real_world_tip: Look at the date in the taskbar first. A date years in the past explains a lot of certificate warnings.
